verdict.line: You lose if you tunnel-vision his Fury bar and get caught by a full empowered combo pre-6; you win if you punish his E (Slice and Dice) cooldown windows and outlast him past level 11.

brief.thesis: This is a 48% win rate over 985 games because both champions win the lane at different windows: Renekton's Fury-empowered all-in peaks hard at level 3 and stays live through level 6, while Aatrox's Q-E trade pattern and item spikes take over from level 11 onward. Neither side is structurally ahead — the 985-game sample and even lane/solo-kill data confirm this comes down to who plays their window correctly, not raw stats.

theirWindow.what: His Q (Cull the Meek), W (Ruthless Predator), and E (Slice and Dice) all empower and his W stun duration doubles. Do not extend trades here — back off after one exchange and let him burn Fury on minions instead of you.

yourWindow.when: His E (Slice and Dice) just landed or is on cooldown
yourWindow.what: Use your Q-E combo the moment his dash is spent — per the matchup read, this is when he can't reposition or disengage. Land Q1 into E (Umbral Dash) gap-close, then finish with Q2/Q3 since he has no answer to the extra mobility.

start.why: Run this on 707 recorded games at 50.9% win rate and 59.9% pick rate — the extra AD and sustain matter more than Doran's Shield's flat damage reduction because your trades with Q1 are burst, not sustained poke, and the lifesteal offsets Renekton's Q (Cull the Meek) sustain race.

boots.why: Picked in 85.8% of games at 48.5% win rate because Renekton's damage is almost entirely physical autos and empowered Q/E — the flat auto-attack reduction directly counters his all-in burst windows.

core.why: Part of the highest-win-rate core path (55.8% over 77 games) — the shield triggers on his empowered all-in and the burst passive punishes him the moment he commits E (Slice and Dice).
Second item in the same 55.8% path — the on-hit heal from Q1 crits stacks your sustain advantage for the level 11+ window where you're already ahead.
Closes out the top-performing build path — the damage-over-time conversion is what lets you win extended trades once his early Fury burst is no longer relevant.

situational.when: he's building tanky and you need to shred through his health pool faster in a longer fight
he rushes armor early to blunt your Q-E burst and you need the shred to keep trading even
you want to close the gap on him faster after he spends E (Slice and Dice) offensively

runes.keystoneWhy: Run on the majority page (50.7% pick, 48.7% win rate) — Conqueror stacks through the extended trades this matchup produces and the healing conversion directly answers Renekton's own Q (Cull the Meek) sustain in prolonged exchanges.

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite is the top pick at 73.1% and posts the best win rate at 50.4% — Ignite denies his Q (Cull the Meek) sustain during your level 3-6 disadvantaged trades and closes out any skirmish where his Fury burst falls short. Flash+Teleport (41.9% win rate, 23.3% pick) is a viable alternative if you expect to be pressured off wave and need to reset.

playing.title: Track Fury before every trade
playing.detail: Never extend a trade once his Fury bar crosses 50 pre-level 6 — his W (Ruthless Predator) stun duration and Q heal both spike hard at that threshold.

playing.title: Poke with Q1 only through level 2
playing.detail: Land the first slash of Q (The Darkin Blade) and disengage rather than chaining into Q2/Q3, since his level 3 all-in threat means committing to a full combo trade is what loses lane.

playing.title: Punish after his E is spent
playing.detail: The instant his E (Slice and Dice) lands or is used to reposition, gap-close with your own E (Umbral Dash) and unload the full Q1-Q2-Q3 sequence — he has no dash to escape it.

playing.title: Use W to wall off his engage
playing.detail: Position near terrain so W (Infernal Chains) can stun him on the follow-up slam if he dashes in with E, converting his engage into your stun window.

playing.title: Freeze the wave levels 1-2
playing.detail: Deny him easy CS and short-trade setups before level 3, since his spike is sharp but late relative to your Q1 poke.

playing.title: Threaten all-in from level 6 after his commit
playing.detail: Once he's already used his empowered W stun on a previous trade, your R (World Ender) turns even skirmishes into kills since he has no follow-up burst left.

playing.title: Play for the level 11+ item spike
playing.detail: Once Eclipse and Sundered Sky are online, actively look for fights rather than farming passively — this is your clearest structural advantage in the matchup.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and win rates above are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch (16.18.1); the power-curve timing and trade-pattern reasoning are my own tactical read of the kits, not sourced from the data.
